must_remember: Diffusion of majority charge carriers across a P-N junction creates a depletion region devoid of mobile carriers but containing immobile ionized donors and acceptors.
In thermal equilibrium, the drift current due to minority carriers exactly balances the diffusion current due to majority carriers, resulting in zero net current.
Under forward bias, the external voltage opposes the barrier potential $V_0$, narrowing the depletion layer and permitting large forward current.
Under reverse bias, the external voltage aids the barrier potential, widening the depletion layer and allowing only a minute reverse saturation current $I_s$.
Transition capacitance $C_T$ arises from stored space-charge in the depletion region under reverse bias, while diffusion capacitance $C_D$ arises from stored minority carriers under forward bias.
The Shockley diode equation is given by $I = I_s \left( \exp\left(\frac{qV}{\eta kT}\right) - 1 \right)$.
Total depletion layer width depends on the applied voltage as $W = \sqrt{\frac{2 \epsilon_s (V_0 - V)}{q} \left(\frac{N_A + N_D}{N_A N_D}\right)}$.

glossary.meaning: The potential difference built across a P-N junction due to space-charge accumulation that stops net diffusion of majority carriers.
A space-charge region near the P-N junction interface containing immobile ionized donors and acceptors, depleted of mobile majority carriers.
Capacitance associated with the voltage-dependent change in space charge within the depletion region of a reverse-biased diode.
Capacitance arising from stored minority carrier charges in neutral regions under forward-bias conditions.
Mathematical relation describing the exponential V-I characteristic of an ideal P-N junction diode.
Small-signal AC resistance of a diode defined as the reciprocal of the slope of its V-I characteristic curve.
